products.title: Aurora Smart 78 — RGB App-Controlled LED
products.body_html:
A 34W RGB LED bar for planted freshwater tanks, set from your phone. 4200 lumens at CRI 90Ra across a 78 cm span, with two bracket heights in the box covering tanks from 70 cm to 95 cm long.

  • Full colour, set from your phone. RGB mixing across the spectrum, adjusted in an app rather than by cycling a button on the cord.
  • Colour you can judge plants by. CRI 90Ra means greens read as greens. Cheap aquarium LEDs sit in the 70s and make a planted tank look flat.
  • 4200 lumens over 78 cm — the second-brightest in the series. Output for every length is in the gallery.
  • Two bracket heights included. Short legs for tanks 70–80 cm, tall legs for 80–95 cm.
  • Aluminium body, IP44 splash rated. Built for the splashes and condensation of an open-top tank, not for submersion.

specs.label: Fits tank length

faqs.q: What size tank does this suit?
faqs.a: The bar is 78 cm long. With the low bracket it suits tanks 70–80 cm long, and with the high bracket 80–95 cm. Both brackets are in the box. On a 95 cm tank the ends of the scape will be noticeably dimmer.

faqs.q: Is 4200 lumens enough for carpeting plants?
faqs.a: For most carpets at this span, yes. We do not publish a PAR figure because the manufacturer does not measure one, and we will not estimate it. If you are growing something genuinely demanding, ask us first.

faqs.q: How is the colour controlled?
faqs.a: Through a phone app over the light's own wireless link. Set the RGB mix once and the fixture keeps it.

faqs.q: Can it get wet?
faqs.a: It is IP44, which covers splashing and condensation on an open-top tank. It is not submersible. An earlier version of this listing claimed IP68 — that was wrong and we have corrected it.

faqs.q: Does it do a sunrise and sunset ramp?
faqs.a: The manufacturer documents no scheduled ramp for this model, so we do not claim one. What is confirmed is app-based colour and brightness control.

products.title: Aurora 48 Planted Tank LED Bar
products.body_html:
A 20W full-spectrum LED bar for planted freshwater tanks between 48 and 58 cm wide (19–23 in). Forty LEDs — thirty daylight white and ten actinic blue — on a retractable bracket, running 90–260V so the same unit works on Australian and US mains.

  • It fits the tank you already own. The bracket slides 10 cm, so one bar covers 48–58 cm of rim. Measure the outside width of the rim, not the water line, and check it against the range before ordering.
  • One unit, either country. 90–260V universal input. No transformer and no voltage-specific variant to get wrong — only the plug head differs.
  • Three modes on an inline switch. All-white for viewing and plant growth, blue-and-white together, or blue alone for a night tank.
  • A timer that repeats. Set the on/off time once and it repeats daily, so light stays consistent while you are away — the main defence against algae from an erratic photoperiod.
  • Slim enough to disappear. A low-profile bar that sits above the rim rather than dominating the tank, in white with translucent blue end caps.

Choosing between lengths. The series runs 18 cm to 58 cm and scales 8W to 24W. Pick by rim width rather than tank volume — a 48 cm bar on a 60 cm tank leaves the ends of the scape visibly dim.
products.tags: src1688:602704953418, planted aquarium lighting, led aquarium light, 20w, 48cm, fits 19-23in, timer, full spectrum

specs.label: Fits tank width
specs.note: Bar length plus 13 cm of bracket travel

specs.label: Input voltage
specs.note: Safe on both 110 V and 240 V mains

faqs.q: Will this fit my tank?
faqs.a: It fits rims from 48 cm to 61 cm (19–24 in). The bar itself is 48 cm and the bracket adds up to 13 cm of travel. Measure the outside width of the rim, not the water line. If your tank is wider than 61 cm, choose the 58 cm model instead.

faqs.q: Will it work on Australian power?
faqs.a: Electrically yes — the driver accepts 90–260 V, so 240 V Australian mains is well within range. Check the plug type on your selected option before ordering; contact us if you need a specific plug and we will confirm what we can supply.

faqs.q: Is it bright enough to grow carpeting plants?
faqs.a: We do not publish a PAR figure for this light because the manufacturer does not provide one, and we will not invent one. What we can state is 20 W across 40 LEDs on a 48 cm bar. If you are growing demanding carpet species, treat this as a low-to-medium light and ask us before ordering.

faqs.q: Does it do a sunrise and sunset fade?
faqs.a: No. It has a repeating on/off timer and three switchable modes, not a gradual ramp. If you specifically want dawn-to-dusk fading, this is not the right fixture.

faqs.q: Can I leave the blue light on overnight?
faqs.a: Yes, the blue-only mode is intended for that. Bear in mind that continuous light of any colour contributes to algae, so most keepers run blue for a few evening hours rather than all night.

faqs.q: What is in the box?
faqs.a: The light bar with both brackets fitted, and the inline switch and power lead attached. No timer plug or wall adapter is included.

products.title: DIY CO2 Generator Kit — 2 L Stainless
products.body_html:
A refill-free CO2 kit for planted tanks. Citric acid and bicarbonate react inside a 2 L stainless bottle to produce CO2 — no gas cylinder, no trips to a refill shop.

  • No cylinder to refill. You top it up with two cheap dry chemicals instead of hauling a bottle to a gas supplier. That is the whole point of this design.
  • Constant-pressure valve body tested above 50 kg/cm² with a 3 kg regulated output and an automatic release above 30 kg.
  • Kit includes the 2 L stainless bottle, pressure gauge and valve, diffuser, 2 m of CO2 tubing, four suction cups, a 300 ml measuring cup, a funnel and two sets of reagent.

What this is not: a pressurised cylinder system. It is a chemical generator. Output tapers as the reaction exhausts and needs recharging every few weeks depending on your bubble rate. If you want set-and-forget pressurised CO2, buy a regulator and a refillable cylinder instead — this is the cheaper, more hands-on route.

images.alt: DIY CO2 Generator Kit — 2 L Stainless
DIY CO2 Generator Kit — 2 L Stainless — view 2

faqs.q: Is this a pressurised CO2 system?
faqs.a: No, and this is the most important thing to understand before buying. It is a chemical generator: citric acid and bicarbonate react to make CO2. There is no cylinder to refill at a gas supplier, but output falls as the reaction exhausts and you recharge it every few weeks. This listing previously described it as a complete CO2 system at $129, which oversold it. We have corrected the description and the price.

faqs.q: How often does it need recharging?
faqs.a: Depends entirely on bubble rate and tank size — commonly two to four weeks on a small tank at a modest rate. The kit ships with two sets of reagent to start.

products.title: Digital pH Pen Meter
products.body_html:
A pocket pH pen for freshwater tanks. Reads 0.00–14.00 pH to 0.1 resolution, runs on two 1.5 V cells, and calibrates against standard buffer powders.

  • pH only. This pen does not measure TDS. An earlier version of this listing said it did; it does not, and we have corrected it.
  • 0.1 pH resolution across the full 0–14 range — enough to track a CO2 swing or a KH change day to day.
  • Two-point calibration against standard buffer sachets, which is what keeps a cheap pen honest over time.

faqs.q: Does this measure TDS?
faqs.a: No. This listing previously said it did — that was wrong and we have corrected it. The unit our supplier ships is a pH-only pen. If you need TDS you need a separate meter, and we would rather lose the sale than send you the wrong tool.

faqs.q: How often does it need calibrating?
faqs.a: Monthly for most tanks, or any time a reading looks implausible. Calibration sachets are cheap and the pen drifts without them.

products.title: Test Strips — 8 in 1, 100 Count
products.body_html:
Eight-parameter dip strips: pH, hardness, ammonia nitrogen, nitrate, nitrite, total chlorine, carbonate and total alkalinity. 100-strip pack.

  • Ammonia and nitrite on the same strip. Those two decide whether a tank is safe to stock. A strip that skips them tells you the least useful things first.
  • Carbonate and total alkalinity separately. KH is what holds pH steady, and it is the number that actually moves when you inject CO2.
  • Dip and read in 30 seconds. Faster than a reagent kit for a weekly check, though a liquid kit is still more precise when you are chasing a problem.
  • 100 strips. At a weekly test that is about two years for one tank.

faqs.q: Are strips as accurate as a liquid test kit?
faqs.a: No. Strips are for spotting a trend quickly. When a reading looks wrong, confirm it with a reagent kit before you act on it.

faqs.q: Does it test CO2?
faqs.a: Not directly, and nor does any strip. Use the KH reading together with pH, or read CO2 off a drop checker.

faqs.q: How should they be stored?
faqs.a: Capped, dry, and away from the tank. Humidity is what ruins strips long before the expiry date does.

products.title: CO2 Solenoid Valve — 12V
products.body_html:
A 12V solenoid that shuts CO2 off with your light timer, so gas is not dosed overnight when plants cannot use it.

  • Stops overnight CO2. Plants only use CO2 under light; dosing in the dark wastes gas and drops pH for nothing.
  • Runs off a standard timer. Wire it inline and let the same schedule that runs your light run your CO2.
  • Low-voltage 12V coil, so no mains voltage near the tank.

specs.label: Function
specs.value: Shuts CO2 off on a timer

faqs.q: Do I need this if my regulator already has a solenoid?
faqs.a: No. This is for regulators without one, or as a spare. Our dual-gauge regulator already includes a solenoid.

products.title: Programmable Auto Feeder
products.body_html:
A rim-mounted feeder with a sealed hopper that drops a measured portion on a schedule you set once. Runs on USB-C or batteries, so a power cut does not mean a missed feed.

  • Two feeds a day, or one. The 12 and 24 hour buttons set the interval; the manual button gives an extra portion without changing the schedule.
  • The hopper stays dry. A sealed drum and a rotating outlet keep humidity off the food, which is what turns cheap feeders into a clogged mess after a fortnight.
  • Portion control. A sliding gate sets how much leaves the drum per turn, so you can tune it to the tank rather than overfeeding and fighting the algae afterwards.
  • Fits rims to 15 mm. The clamp takes both open-top and braced rims, and the arm angles so the outlet clears the glass.

images.alt: Programmable Auto Feeder with rim clamp
Programmable Auto Feeder hopper loaded with pellets, dispensing

faqs.q: Will it work with flake food?
faqs.a: Yes. Flake needs the gate opened wider than pellets because it bridges more easily. Set the gate, watch one cycle, then adjust.

faqs.q: What happens in a blackout?
faqs.a: It keeps its schedule on the internal cell or the AAAs. That is the reason to pick a battery-backed feeder over a mains one.

faqs.q: Is it safe to leave for a week away?
faqs.a: For a week, yes, provided you run it for a few days first and confirm the portion size. Do not set a feeder for the first time the day you leave.

products.title: Digital Thermometer with Probe
products.body_html:
A stick-on LCD with a sealed probe on a one-metre lead. It reads to 0.1 °C and remembers the high and low since you last cleared it, which is how you catch a heater that is drifting at night.

  • Max and min memory. A spot reading tells you nothing about the overnight swing. This holds both extremes until you reset it.
  • Probe in the water, display outside. No hunting for an angle to read a glass thermometer through a planted foreground.
  • 0.1 °C resolution, °C or °F. Fine enough to see the difference between a stable tank and a heater cycling too wide.
  • Suction cup and adhesive pad. Mount the display on the cabinet or the glass, and route the probe behind the hardscape.

images.alt: Digital Thermometer with probe and suction cup

faqs.q: Is the probe fully submersible?
faqs.a: The probe and its lead are sealed for permanent submersion. The display housing is not — keep it outside the tank.

faqs.q: Why does it read differently to my glass thermometer?
faqs.a: Usually because they are in different places. Water stratifies, especially in a tank with low flow. Put both in the same spot for a fair comparison.

faqs.q: Can I calibrate it?
faqs.a: No, it is a fixed ±1 °C sensor. For stability tracking that is plenty; if you need certified accuracy you want a lab probe.

products.title: Fine-Mesh Fish Net — Braided Handle
products.body_html:
A soft fine-mesh net on a braided stainless handle. The mesh is fine enough for shrimp and fry, and soft enough not to tear a long fin.

  • Fine mesh, soft weave. Coarse nets catch shrimp legs and split betta fins. This one does not.
  • Square mouth. Corners are where fish escape a round net. A square profile works into the corner of the glass.
  • Braided handle, not stamped. Stamped handles bend and the join rusts. Braided stainless does not stain hardscape.

images.alt: Fine-mesh aquarium fish net with braided stainless handle

image.alt: Fine-mesh aquarium fish net with braided stainless handle

faqs.q: Will it hold shrimp?
faqs.a: Yes. The weave is fine enough that adult and juvenile shrimp do not pass through or get a leg caught.

faqs.q: Can it be left wet?
faqs.a: Rinse in tank water and air-dry. Do not use soap on it — residue is far more dangerous to a tank than a damp net.

products.title: Intake Pre-Filter Sponge — 9 Pack
products.body_html:
Nine slip-on foam sleeves for a filter intake. They stop fry, shrimp and plant trimmings being drawn into the impeller, and they carry a useful bacterial load once they are established.

  • Shrimp and fry safety. The usual reason a shrimp disappears is the intake. A sleeve solves it outright.
  • Extra biological media. An established sponge is colonised, so rinse it in tank water, never under the tap.
  • Nine of them. Rotate: run one while another dries, and you never strip the filter of bacteria in one go.
  • Fits intakes to about 25 mm. Stretches over most internal filter and canister intakes.

images.alt: Nine-pack of foam pre-filter sponge sleeves for aquarium filter intakes

image.alt: Nine-pack of foam pre-filter sponge sleeves for aquarium filter intakes

faqs.q: How often should they be cleaned?
faqs.a: When flow drops noticeably, usually every week or two in a planted tank. Squeeze it out in a jug of tank water.

faqs.q: Will it reduce my filter flow?
faqs.a: Slightly, and more as it loads up. That is the trade for keeping shrimp out of the impeller.

products.title: Acrylic Breeder Box — Hang-On
products.body_html:
A clear acrylic box that hangs inside the tank on suction cups, with a divided lower chamber and a slotted floor so fry drop away from the adult.

  • Fry drop through, adults cannot follow. The slotted floor is the whole point of a breeder box — it separates them at birth without you watching.
  • Shares the tank's water. No separate heater, no separate cycle, and no shock when the fry are eventually released.
  • Divided chamber. Also serves as an isolation box for a fish being treated or a fin recovering.

images.alt: Clear acrylic hang-on aquarium breeder box with suction cups

image.alt: Clear acrylic hang-on aquarium breeder box with suction cups

faqs.q: Does it need its own heater?
faqs.a: No. It hangs in the tank and shares its water and temperature, which is the main advantage over a separate tank.

faqs.q: Will the fry get enough flow?
faqs.a: Position it near, not directly in front of, the filter outlet. Fry need gentle exchange, not a current.

products.title: Glass Lily Pipe Set — Inflow & Outflow
products.body_html:
A matched pair of borosilicate glass pipes that replace the black plastic intake and spraybar most filters ship with. The outflow returns water in a rolling surface curve; the slotted inflow draws evenly without pinning fish against it.

  • The reason aquascapers switch. Glass disappears against the background. Plastic intakes are the single most visible piece of hardware in an otherwise clean tank.
  • Surface agitation without a ripple tank. The outflow curve breaks the surface film and helps gas exchange, which matters more once you are injecting CO2.
  • Slotted intake. Wide slots pass debris to the filter instead of clogging, and keep shrimp and fry out of the impeller.
  • Borosilicate, not soda-lime. Thicker walls and better thermal tolerance. Still glass — see the FAQ on cleaning.
products.tags: tools, equipment, glassware, planted tank, aquascaping

images.alt: Glass lily pipe set, inflow with slotted intake and curved outflow

image.alt: Glass lily pipe set, inflow with slotted intake and curved outflow

faqs.q: How do I clean the inside?
faqs.a: A flexible pipe brush, or soak in a dilute bleach solution then rinse and dechlorinate thoroughly. Do not run wire down it — scratched glass is where the next crack starts.

faqs.q: Will it fit my filter?
faqs.a: Match the tubing bore, not the filter brand. 12/16 mm suits most small canisters, 16/22 mm the larger ones. Measure your existing hose if unsure.

faqs.q: Is glass a risk?
faqs.a: Honestly, yes — it is the trade for the look. The common failure is over-tightening a hose onto the pipe or knocking it against the rim during a water change, not spontaneous breakage.

products.title: Stainless Lily Pipe Set — Inflow & Outflow
products.body_html:
The same geometry as a glass lily pipe set in 304 stainless. It gives up the invisibility of glass and gets back the one thing glass cannot offer: you can knock it against the rim and nothing happens.

  • For tanks that get worked on. If you rescape often, or the tank is somewhere it gets bumped, this is the set that survives it.
  • 304, not 201. The cheaper grade spots and bleeds rust into hardscape within months in fresh water. 304 does not.
  • Reads as intentional. Brushed steel against a rimless tank looks deliberate in a way black plastic never does.
  • Same slotted intake. Debris passes to the filter, shrimp and fry stay out of the impeller.
products.tags: tools, equipment, glassware, planted tank, aquascaping

images.alt: Stainless steel lily pipe set, inflow and outflow with clamps

image.alt: Stainless steel lily pipe set, inflow and outflow with clamps

faqs.q: Glass or stainless?
faqs.a: Glass if the tank is a display piece and stays undisturbed. Stainless if you rescape regularly or the tank lives somewhere it gets knocked.

faqs.q: Will stainless rust?
faqs.a: 304 will not in fresh water. Avoid steel wool on it — embedded iron particles are what usually causes 'stainless' to spot.

faqs.q: Is it as quiet as glass?
faqs.a: Yes. Flow noise comes from the water level and the outflow angle, not the material. Sit the outflow just under the surface.
